label: <DEL> step when the sequence starts with p/g/q/2/i/3
explanation: Fires mainly on the delimiter step (88% of activation mass; about 10% of <DEL> steps are active), i.e. when the first original token is about to be output. Whether it fires there depends on which tokens opened the sequence: strongly enriched when first_tok (= the token output at <DEL>) is p, g, q or 2 (lift about 4x), weaker for i, 3, s, t, u, y, b. When both of the first two originals are in {p,g,q,2,i,3}, the <DEL> step is active with 84% precision but recall drops to 27%. It is a graded readout of several early tokens, so no simple predicate gets above F1 of about 0.48. Activation is somewhat higher for longer sequences (L=8-9). Secondary: about 12% of mass sits in the original phase, mostly on input e (and some h/n/o/r) late in long sequences. Almost never active in the copy phase after <DEL> or at t=0.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: p, q, g, 2, i, 3; least: x, o, f, r) and the next token to output (most: g, p, q, 2, i, 3; least: x, o, f, e); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, L=5 & t=9.
